source.ten: Reference compilation (editorial draft, 2026) following Chaldean numerology — Cheiro, Book of Numbers (1926)
source.luu_y: Editorial draft retold in our own words, not copied from the book; shown by decision of the project owner (2026-09-30), with a status column for gradual review. A cultural reference, not a forecast.

gioi_thieu.tom_tat: By tradition, the Chaldean system of numerology goes back to ancient Babylon, and Cheiro made it popular in English in the early twentieth century. Each letter carries a value from 1 to 8 according to its sound, while 9 is kept apart as a sacred number and given to no letter. This school puts weight on the name other people usually call you and on the symbolic meaning of compound numbers.
khac_pitago: A different letter table: letters get values from 1 to 8 by sound and vibration, not in A, B, C order as in Pythagorean numerology.
No letter carries the number 9; 9 only appears when the totals are added up.
The compound numbers 10–52 have their own symbolic meanings, read before reducing to the root number.
The everyday name (the one you hear most) counts for more than the full name on official papers.
No birth chart grid, arrows or pinnacles as in Pythagorean numerology.
No master numbers: 11 and 22 are only read as compound numbers, then reduced to 2 and 4.
gioi_thieu.cach_doc: The root number shows the main tendency; the compound number adds a shade of meaning and a symbolic image to that tendency. It is a prompt for reflection, not a prediction about anyone's life.

1.xu_huong: In the Chaldean tradition, 1 is usually described as an opening source of energy that likes to set its own direction and take the lead. People with this number are often said to decide quickly and to dislike waiting for someone else's approval.
1.mat_toi: Can treat their own view as the only right one and overlook the quiet people in the group.
1.goi_y: This week, before a group decision, ask the person who speaks least for their view before you give yours.
1.cau_tu_soi: Did you decide something for the group last week without asking anyone?

2.xu_huong: 2 is usually described as gentle, imaginative and sensitive to the mood around it. Tradition links this number to the Moon, so it stresses changing feelings and the ability to read other people.
2.mat_toi: Can go along with others so much that they never say what they really want, then feel quietly resentful.
2.goi_y: This week, pick one moment when you were about to say 'whatever you like' and give a concrete choice of your own instead.
2.cau_tu_soi: Was the last time you turned down a request this week?

3.xu_huong: 3 is linked to Jupiter, so it is usually described as reaching for growth and learning, with the ambition to rise. People with this number are often said to enjoy organising and teaching others what they know.
3.mat_toi: Can take on too many plans at once and care more about the title than about finishing.
3.goi_y: This week, cross off one thing you agreed to do but no longer really want to.
3.cau_tu_soi: Are you chasing more than three plans, none of them finished yet?

4.xu_huong: In the Chaldean school, 4 is usually described as seeing things from an unusual angle and questioning the usual way of doing things. People with this number are often said to work persistently, but in their own way.
4.mat_toi: Can object out of habit, so others hesitate to put ideas on the table.
4.goi_y: This week, when you are about to disagree with an idea, first name one point in it that makes sense to you.
4.cau_tu_soi: At your last meeting or family meal, did you push back on someone's idea before hearing it out?

5.xu_huong: 5 is linked to Mercury, so it is usually described as quick-witted, well-spoken and fond of a change of scene. People with this number are often said to learn fast and make friends easily, but to get bored when things repeat.
5.mat_toi: Can drop things once the novelty wears off, and promise more than they can keep up with.
5.goi_y: This week, choose one unfinished task and give it a whole session to move it to the next step.
5.cau_tu_soi: Did you give up on a course or a new habit you started this month?

6.xu_huong: 6 is linked to Venus, so it is usually described as loving beauty, valuing harmony and drawing people in. People with this number are often said to take care of their home, their friends and the atmosphere around them.
6.mat_toi: Can avoid necessary friction to keep things looking pleasant, or take on other people's tasks for fear of upsetting them.
6.goi_y: This week, tell someone close, gently, about one thing that bothers you instead of staying silent.
6.cau_tu_soi: Did you take over someone else's task last week just to avoid tension?

7.xu_huong: 7 is linked to Neptune, so it is usually described as intuitive, reflective and drawn to things that are hard to measure. People with this number are often said to love travel and deep reading, and to need quiet time of their own.
7.mat_toi: Can drift into imagination and put off the practical tasks in front of them.
7.goi_y: This week, write down an idea you have been nursing for a long time, together with one small step you can take within two days.
7.cau_tu_soi: Have you been putting off some paperwork or a household task for more than a week?

8.xu_huong: 8 is linked to Saturn, so it is usually described as serious, able to bear long pressure and to go the distance through persistence. People with this number are often said to show little of themselves and to be mistaken for cold.
8.mat_toi: Can carry everything alone, not share difficulties and be harder on themselves than they need to be.
8.goi_y: This week, tell someone you trust about something that is weighing on you.
8.cau_tu_soi: Last week, did you ask anyone for help with something that felt like too much?

9.xu_huong: 9 is linked to Mars, so it is usually described as energetic, willing to face things head-on and keen to defend what it believes in. The Chaldean tradition treats 9 as a sacred number that only appears in totals and is never given to a letter.
9.mat_toi: Can be impatient, speak sharply when blocked and act before hearing everything.
9.goi_y: This week, when you feel irritated, take one long breath before you reply to that message or remark.
9.cau_tu_soi: Last week, did you send a message while annoyed and then regret it?

10.xu_huong: In the Chaldean tradition this compound number is pictured as a turning wheel: ups and downs in turn, and the ability to start again after each round. It is often linked to self-confidence and to being remembered by name.
10.mat_toi: Can lean on good circumstances and neglect to prepare for when the wheel turns.
10.cau_tu_soi: When a plan falls apart, do you start over within a week?

11.xu_huong: By tradition this compound number is pictured as a clenched hand or a lion held in check: the strength is there but being held back. The theme is learning to trust the right people and to say clearly what you want.
11.mat_toi: Can be overly suspicious of others or, the other way round, quick to believe fine promises.
11.cau_tu_soi: Do you check an important promise in writing before relying on it?

12.xu_huong: This compound number is usually pictured as someone who willingly sets aside their own needs to serve someone else's goals. The traditional theme is learning the difference between helping and being taken advantage of.
12.mat_toi: Can take the short end of the stick and then feel hurt without saying so.
12.cau_tu_soi: This month, have you said 'no' to a request for unpaid extra work?

13.xu_huong: The Chaldean tradition links this compound number to changes of plan, home or way of life: the old closes so the new has room. It is often read as an invitation to clear things out yourself rather than cling on.
13.mat_toi: Can rush into change and throw out things that still have value just out of boredom.
13.cau_tu_soi: Are you holding on to a habit or an object you haven't used for more than a year?

14.xu_huong: This compound number is usually described as constant movement, meeting and bringing people and tasks together — suited to trade, exchange and travel. The theme is staying careful when everything moves fast.
14.mat_toi: Can bet on other people's word without looking into things themselves.
14.cau_tu_soi: The last time you agreed to put money or effort into a venture, did you read the terms carefully yourself?

15.xu_huong: By tradition this compound number is linked to a gift for words, charm and persuasion, with others glad to help. It is often described as a magnetism that can be used to lift people up or to get your own way.
15.mat_toi: Can use their charm to get what they want and forget to ask whether the other person truly agrees.
15.cau_tu_soi: Last week, did you talk someone into something they were still unsure about?

16.xu_huong: The Chaldean tradition pictures this compound number as a tower struck by lightning: an old structure that no longer fits has to make way. It is often read as a theme of rebuilding on a more honest, more modest foundation.
16.mat_toi: Can cling to a set plan even when many signs say it needs adjusting.
16.cau_tu_soi: Are you carrying on with a plan only because you have already put so much effort into it?

17.xu_huong: Tradition calls this compound number the star of the Magi: a steady spirit that overcomes trials to leave its mark. It is often linked to perseverance and the wish to be remembered.
17.mat_toi: Can be so taken up with their long-term image that they overlook the people beside them today.
17.cau_tu_soi: This week, have you given someone close a whole session without looking at your phone?

18.xu_huong: By tradition this compound number carries the image of the moon shining on two shores: a tug between material desire and inner life. The theme is noticing the conflict inside before it becomes a conflict outside.
18.mat_toi: Can misread people close to them and keep grievances to themselves until they burst out.
18.cau_tu_soi: Have you been angry with someone lately without telling them why?

19.xu_huong: Tradition calls this compound number the prince of heaven: light, recognition and the joy of having your efforts seen. It is often described as favourable for setting a clear goal and seeing it through.
19.mat_toi: Can grow complacent when praised and shy away from criticism.
19.cau_tu_soi: The last time you got feedback, did you ask for details instead of explaining yourself again?

20.xu_huong: The Chaldean tradition links this compound number to awakening: a call towards a new purpose and new plans. It is often read as a good moment to look again at what you really want to pursue.
20.mat_toi: Can hear the call but put it off while waiting for perfect conditions.
20.cau_tu_soi: Is there a plan you have been thinking about for more than six months without taking the first step?

21.xu_huong: This compound number is usually pictured as the crown of maturity: results that come after a long road and many trials. The theme is patience and trust in the process.
21.mat_toi: Can think they have arrived and stop learning.
21.cau_tu_soi: This month, have you learned a new skill outside your usual work?

22.xu_huong: By tradition this compound number carries the image of a traveller lost in a daydream, trusting others and forgetting to watch the road. The theme is keeping your ideals while still checking reality yourself.
22.mat_toi: Can let others make important decisions for them.
22.cau_tu_soi: Have you looked over your household spending yourself this month?

23.xu_huong: Tradition calls this compound number the royal star of the Lion: support from people in positions of influence, and favour for your own plans. It is often linked to confidence in presenting ideas.
23.mat_toi: Can wait for others to open doors and prepare little themselves.
23.cau_tu_soi: The last time you had a chance to present an idea, did you prepare it on paper beforehand?

24.xu_huong: The Chaldean tradition links this compound number to affection, creativity and help from those who came before. It is often described as good relationships opening doors that effort alone would struggle to open.
24.mat_toi: Can rely on connections and forget to build real ability.
24.cau_tu_soi: Last week, did you thank someone specifically for helping you?

25.xu_huong: This compound number is usually described as strength formed through observation and experience, including the stumbles. The theme is turning old lessons into new steadiness.
25.mat_toi: Can hold on to unhappy memories and keep retelling them.
25.cau_tu_soi: After something went wrong recently, did you write down what you learned?

26.xu_huong: By tradition this compound number points to business ties or partnerships that need careful thought. It is often read as a theme of choosing who you work with and spelling out responsibilities from the start.
26.mat_toi: Can agree to help out of politeness without setting clear conditions.
26.cau_tu_soi: The last time you worked in a group, did you agree out loud on who does what?

27.xu_huong: Tradition pictures this compound number as a sceptre: authority that comes from independent thinking and your own creativity. It is often described as favourable when you trust a plan of your own that you have thought through.
27.mat_toi: Can become rigid, believing their way is the only way.
27.cau_tu_soi: This week, did you try doing a familiar task the way someone else suggested?

28.xu_huong: The Chaldean tradition links this compound number to contradictions: a promising start, but care is needed in placing your trust. The theme is rebuilding through your own effort instead of relying on others.
28.mat_toi: Can stake a whole plan on one person's promise.
28.cau_tu_soi: Do you have a backup plan for the important thing that currently depends on someone else?

29.xu_huong: This compound number is usually described through uncertainty in relationships and moments when it is hard to tell true from false. By tradition the theme is learning to listen to your intuition and to ask directly rather than guess.
29.mat_toi: Can read things into what others mean and react to what they imagined.
29.cau_tu_soi: The last time you felt suspicious of someone, did you ask them directly?

30.xu_huong: By tradition this compound number is linked to thoughtful reasoning, looking back and putting the mind above material things. People with it are often described as preferring to watch from the side rather than compete.
30.mat_toi: Can seem distant, so people close to them find them hard to approach.
30.cau_tu_soi: Last week, did you invite anyone to meet up?

31.xu_huong: Tradition pictures this compound number as someone self-sufficient, living by their own principles and needing the crowd very little. The theme is balancing independence with connection.
31.mat_toi: Can withdraw so far that they miss support that is already there.
31.cau_tu_soi: This month, have you turned down more than two invitations to get together?

32.xu_huong: The Chaldean tradition links this compound number to the power of communication and the ability to rally many people around an idea. It is often described as favourable when you hold on to your own judgement.
32.mat_toi: Can get carried along by the majority and forget what they had carefully thought through.
32.cau_tu_soi: The last time the whole group opposed your idea, did you stand by it, with your reasons?

33.xu_huong: By tradition this compound number has no shade of its own but carries the spirit of support and warm affection. It is often read as a theme of passing on the help you once received.
33.mat_toi: Can help on impulse and then drop it when busy.
33.cau_tu_soi: This month, have you kept one small promise to help someone?

34.xu_huong: Tradition groups this compound number with the spirit of strength from experience. It is often read as a theme of sharing your lessons so those who come after stumble less.
34.mat_toi: Can give too much advice when the other person only needs to be heard.
34.cau_tu_soi: The last time someone confided in you, did you listen to the end without slipping in advice?

35.xu_huong: By tradition this compound number brings the theme of careful thought in any alliance. It is often read as a reminder to keep clear boundaries about money with people you know.
35.mat_toi: Can mix friendship and business until it is hard to talk straight.
35.cau_tu_soi: Have you lent something or money to someone you know without agreeing on when you will get it back?

36.xu_huong: Tradition groups this compound number with the spirit of the sceptre: authority from independent thinking. It is often described as favourable for travelling and learning outside familiar ground.
36.mat_toi: Can feel lonely at the front without saying so.
36.cau_tu_soi: This year, have you gone somewhere new purely to learn?

37.xu_huong: In the Chaldean tradition this compound number is linked to good friendship, harmonious affection and partnership between two people. It is often described as favourable for working in pairs rather than alone.
37.mat_toi: Can depend on one close friend and do little to widen their circle.
37.cau_tu_soi: This month, have you got to know someone new outside your usual group of friends?

38.xu_huong: Tradition groups this compound number with the theme of trust being tested. It is often read as a reminder to state your expectations in a relationship instead of waiting for others to understand.
38.mat_toi: Can feel let down when others don't guess what they need.
38.cau_tu_soi: Last week, did you say a wish clearly to someone close instead of waiting for them to notice?

39.xu_huong: By tradition this compound number carries the spirit of thinking things over and looking back. It is often described as suited to writing, research or putting your thoughts in order.
39.mat_toi: Can think for so long that the moment to act passes.
39.cau_tu_soi: Is there a decision you have weighed for more than a month without settling it?

40.xu_huong: Tradition groups this compound number with the spirit of the self-sufficient person. It is often read as a theme of keeping your own rhythm amid many outside demands.
40.mat_toi: Can see asking for help as weakness.
40.cau_tu_soi: Last week, did you ask someone to do a small thing you could easily have done yourself?

41.xu_huong: By tradition this compound number carries the power of communication and the ability to gather people. It is often described as favourable for teaching, public speaking or writing for a wide readership.
41.mat_toi: Can talk more than they do, so their words lose weight.
41.cau_tu_soi: This month, have you finished what you announced in front of everyone?

42.xu_huong: Tradition groups this compound number with the spirit of affection and support. It is often read as a theme of looking after long-standing relationships.
42.mat_toi: Can take the care of people close to them for granted.
42.cau_tu_soi: This week, have you called someone you haven't been in touch with for a long time?

43.xu_huong: The Chaldean tradition links this compound number to upheaval and revolution: the old order is called into question. It is often read as a theme of daring to change how you work when the old way no longer works.
43.mat_toi: Can tear everything down at once instead of changing it part by part.
43.cau_tu_soi: The last time you wanted to change something, did you break it into small steps?

44.xu_huong: By tradition this compound number sits close to the theme of partnerships that need careful thought. It is often read as a reminder to check the foundations of something before building more on it.
44.mat_toi: Can expand too fast while the core is still loose.
44.cau_tu_soi: Do you review your unfinished tasks before taking on new ones?

45.xu_huong: By tradition this compound number carries the spirit of the sceptre: authority built through consistency. It is often described as favourable when you keep your word over a long time.
45.mat_toi: Can be hard on people who don't keep up with their standards.
45.cau_tu_soi: Last week, did you patiently show someone again how to do something they had got wrong?

46.xu_huong: Tradition groups this compound number with the spirit of friendship and harmonious partnership. It is often read as a theme that things are lighter done together than alone.
46.mat_toi: Can avoid disagreeing with a close friend even when something needs saying.
46.cau_tu_soi: Have you given a close friend honest feedback lately?

47.xu_huong: By tradition this compound number carries the theme of telling apart what is true from what you wish were true. It is often read as a reminder to check information before believing it.
47.mat_toi: Can trust a first impression and ignore facts that point the other way.
47.cau_tu_soi: Before sharing a piece of news online recently, did you check the source?

48.xu_huong: Tradition groups this compound number with the spirit of reflection. It is often read as a theme of stepping back to see the whole picture before reacting.
48.mat_toi: Can stick to watching and commenting and shy away from getting their hands dirty.
48.cau_tu_soi: This week, did you do something yourself that you used to only comment on?

49.xu_huong: By tradition this compound number carries the spirit of the self-sufficient person. It is often described as favourable for teaching yourself, doing things yourself and owning your choices.
49.mat_toi: Can reject advice simply because they want to decide for themselves.
49.cau_tu_soi: The last time someone gave you sound advice, did you follow it?

50.xu_huong: Tradition groups this compound number with the spirit of connecting words. It is often read as a theme of exchanging ideas and learning from people in other fields.
50.mat_toi: Can spread themselves thin by talking with too many people at once.
50.cau_tu_soi: Today, did you turn off notifications to finish one task completely?

51.xu_huong: The Chaldean tradition links this compound number to the figure of the warrior: strength, rapid advance and the courage to take on hard work. It is often described as favourable for people building their own place in the world.
51.mat_toi: Can treat everyone else as a rival and create needless tension.
51.cau_tu_soi: Last week, did you compete with someone over something small?

52.xu_huong: Tradition groups this compound number with the theme of great upheaval. It is often read as an invitation to review habits that have outlived their use and replace them with something that fits better.
52.mat_toi: Can keep an old way of working just because their hands are used to it.
52.cau_tu_soi: Have you changed any of your working habits this month?
